questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct for the given floral diagrams?
options: 'A' shows the floral diagram of Family Solanaceae, while 'B' shows the floral diagram of Family Fabaceae.

The floral formula of ' $\mathrm{A}$ ' is $\% \sigma^* \mathrm{~K}_{(5)} \mathrm{C}_{1+2+(2)} \mathrm{A}_{(9)+1} \underline{\mathrm{G}}_1$, while that of ' $\mathrm{B}$ ' is $\oplus \sigma_{+}^{\prime} \mathrm{K}_{(5)} \overbrace{(5)} \mathrm{A}_5 \underline{G}_{(2)}$.
The fruits of both 'A' and 'B' are berry or capsule.
Physalis and Atropa belong to 'A', while Sesbania and Trifolium belong to 'B'.
questions.solution: ' $A$ ' and ' $B$ ' show the floral diagrams of Family Fabaceae and Solanaceae, respectively. Sesbania and Trifolium belong to Family Fabaceae while Physalis and Atropa belong to Family Solanaceae. Fruit of Fabaceae may be legume or lomentum whereas fruit of Solanaceae may be berry or capsule.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The endosperm in gymnosperm is formed after fertilisation.
Reason : The endosperm of gymnosperm is formed by triple fusion.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In gymnosperm, the female gametophyte is known as endosperm. It is haploid in nature. It is a food laden tissue in seed for future growth of embryo. The endosperm in gymnosperm is developed before fertilisation. The endosperm of angiosperm is formed after fertilisation by triple fusion.

questions.q:
Assertion : A mangrove tree growing in marshy place has pneumatophores.
Reason : Pneumatophores help in better anchorage to marshy soil.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Mangroves which form shallow littoral forests near sea shores areas are halophytes. Mangrove grow in physiologically dry environment (water is available in plenty but in the form of strong salt solution). These plants develop shallow rootings due to water logged environment where oxygen scarcity prevails. To ensure proper aeration in root system, plants produce respiratory roots or pneumatophores which are negatively geotropic peg-like projections above ground with numerous pores or lenticels for gaseous exchange:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cotton fibres mainly contains
questions.solution: The cotton fibres represent epidermal prolongations of seed coat cells. A raw cotton fibre, on average, gives the following values on analysis : cellulose, $94 \%$, protein - $1.3 \%$, pectic substances $-0.9 \%$, ash $-1.2 \%$, wax $-0.6 \%$, sugars $-0.3 \%$ and traces of pigments and mineral matter.

Spadix is a racemose inflorescence having pendulous spike with main axis much flattened.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cells of the quiescent centre are characterised by
options: having dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
having light cytoplasm and small nuclei
dividing regularly to add to the corpus
dividing regularly to add to tunica
questions.solution: In the apices of some roots, (e.g., Zea mays, maize), there is a central region of cells which normally does not divide. This central inactive region was called quiescent centre by F.A.L. Clowes $(1959,1961)$. The cells of this region have lesser amounts of RNA and DNA so they have small nuclei. These cells also have a lower rate of protein synthesis. Mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum are less developed. The cells of the quiescent centre are usually inactive. However, if already existing meristematic cells are injured or become inactive due to any other reason, the cells of quiescent centre become active.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Upon fertilization, what structure develops from carpel?
questions.solution: Ripened ovary or fertilized ovary is called fruit. The wall of the ovary forms fleshy or dry fruit wall known as pericarp. It means that the pericarp is developed from pistil or carpel.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Maize is an albuminous seed.
Reason : Endosperm is completely absorbed by its growing embryo.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Any seed which contains endosperm or perisperm at maturity is called albuminous or endospermic seed i.e., food reserve of the seed is stored in endosperm or perisperm, e.g. rubber, coconut, castor bean, maize and other cereals. Seed that does not have endosperm at maturity and in which cotyledons absorb food reserve from endosperm during development and act as storage organs is called exalbuminous or nonendospermic seed, e.g., mustard, groundnut, bean, pea etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Nuclear endosperm is formed by subsequent nuclear division without wall formation.
Reason : Coconut is an example of such endosperm, where the endosperm remains nuclear throughout the development of the fruit.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In nuclear endosperm, first and further divisions of primary endosperm nucleus are not followed by cytokinesis or wall formation and thus these free nuclear divisions lead to formation of a large number of free nuclei in embryo sac. At maturity, centripetal wall formation may occur to make the tissue partly cellular. Endosperm of coconut is unique in sense that it is both nuclear and cellular. Here the primary endosperm nucleus undergoes a number of free nuclear divisions. When the fruit is about $50 \mathrm{~mm}$ long the embryo sac remains filled with a watery fluid or milk containing free nuclei and fine cytoplasmic particles. At a later stage when the fruit becomes about $100 \mathrm{~mm}$ in length the liquid shows in addition to free nuclei, several cells each enclosing variable number of nuclei. Thus coconut has multicellular endosperm (called coconut meat) in the outer part and free nuclear as well as vacuolate endosperm (called coconut milk) in the centre.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Velamen present in orchids helps in
options: absorption of nutrients from host plant
questions.solution: Some epiphytes eg., orchids have aerial roots. In these roots, the outer covering is made up of a spongy tissue called velamen which absorbs moisture from the air. Thus, the aerial plant can prepare food by photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Composite fruit develops from
questions.solution: Composite fruits are multiple fruits which are developed from the complete inflorescence and are also called as infructescence. They are of two types sorosis and syconus. Spike, spadix and catkin type of inflorescence gives rise to this type of fruit eg Ananas, Artocarpus. Syconus develops from a hypanthodium inflorescence eg Ficus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The family containing mustard and its main characters are
options: Brassicaceae - Tetramerous flowers, six stamens, bicarpellary gynoecium, siliqua type fruit
Brassicaceae - Pentamerous flowers, many stamens, pentacarpellary gynoecium, capsule type fruit
Solanaceae - Pentamerous flowers, five stamens, bicarpellary gynoecium, berry type fruit
Poaceae - Trimerous flowers, three stamens, monocarpellary gynoecium, caryopsis type of fruit.
questions.solution: Brassica (mustard) belongs to family Brassicaceae. Family brassicaceae is characterised by polypetalous 4 petals, polysepalous 4 sepals, six stamens (which are in tetradynamous condition i.e. 4 +2 or in two whorls, 4 inner long and 2 outer short). Gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous unilocular with parietal placentation. Fruit is usually siliqua (dry dehiscent fruit formed by bicarpellary syncarpous gynoecium with replum) and rarely lomentum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The two cotyledons in the seed are often referred to as the embryonic leaves.
Reason : The embryo contains radicle and plumule.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In a typical angiospermic plant, cotyledons in the seed are the embryonic leaves. The radicle of the embryo upon the seed germination produces the root system and the plumule produces the shoot system. The radicle and plumule are contained in the embryo.

questions.solution: In tetradynamous condition there is $4+2$ arrangement of stamens i.e., out of six stamens, 4 are long and 2 are short. It is a characterstic feature of members of family Brassicaceae.
